first.rationale: Current situation shows dual pressure: activation down 6% QoQ and competitor taking price-sensitive SMB share. Memory_73 established promotional pricing as effective for SMB acquisition and revenue lift; memory_31 showed signup simplification drove activation lift. Verifying memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing efficacy and revenue impact specifics) and memory_31 (whether activation lift persisted and under what conditions) is critical because: (1) promotional pricing directly addresses the competitive threat and price sensitivity, (2) it is a high-consequence lever for qualified revenue, and (3) the interaction between pricing and activation quality is under-specified in current memory. A small guarded test on promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB cohorts can address the competitive threat while preserving the option to pivot to activation-focused interventions (memory_91, memory_86) if pricing proves counterproductive to long-term unit economics. Flagging downstream risk: aggressive pricing may compress margins or attract lower-LTV cohorts; guarded test scale mitigates this. Preserving uncertainty: test will generate signal on whether price sensitivity is the primary driver of current activation decline or whether product/messaging changes are needed.

final.rationale: Archive verification reveals critical insight: memory_73's promotional pricing drove +31% signup but -12% 30-day retention—the acquired cohort does not survive renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing as a lever for sustainable long-term qualified revenue despite short-term acquisition lift. The competitor threat is real but promotional pricing reproduces the same cohort-quality problem. Memory_31 showed signup simplification produced +9% activation with only -1% retention impact, suggesting activation itself is the true constraint, not price. Current activation decline (-6% QoQ) combined with onboarding completion decline (-4% QoQ) points to product engagement friction, not acquisition friction. Memory_91 (activation messaging improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action) and memory_86 (shortening onboarding lifted adoption across self-serve) together suggest a path to recover activation without sacrificing cohort quality or renewal durability. Standard_experiment scale allows rigorous measurement of activation messaging impact on both engagement and downstream retention. This preserves long-term revenue quality while directly addressing the observed activation decline, and avoids the retention cliff that memory_73 revealed in discounting strategies.
